injuryReports.name: Kyle Dugger
injuryReports.returnComment: Dugger drew the questionable tag for Monday Night Football, but the veteran safety will end up missing a fourth consecutive game due to a quadriceps injury. He logged full practices during Week 11 prep, so there's a chance he makes his return in Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Dax Hill
injuryReports.returnComment: Hill was absent from practice for the entire week due to an illness, but he is now good to go for Monday Night Football. The 26-year-old will operate in his starting role at slot cornerback versus Washington.
injuryReports.injury: Hill (illness) is active for Monday night's contest against the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Jalen Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: Davis strung together multiple full practices since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 12, but he still drew the doubtful tag for Monday's game. He'll end up missing a seventh consecutive game due to a hamstring injury, and his next chance to return is Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Andrei Iosivas
injuryReports.returnComment: Iosivas will remain on injured reserve for at least one more week, after the Bengals had listed him as doubtful heading into Monday's contest following a trio of full practices from Thursday through Saturday. If the fourth-year wideout can turn in another full slate of practices in Week 12, he should have a better chance of being restored to the 53-man roster ahead of the Bengals' Nov. 29 matchup with the Saints.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: Joe Burrow
injuryReports.returnComment: Burrow dealt with an illness during Week 11 prep, but with no injury tag the 2020 first overall pick has been officially cleared to play Monday night -- and per ESPN.com he is confident he will do so at "full strength." He's thrown at least three touchdowns in each of his last five outings, and over that span he has completed 77.6 percent of his passes for 1,624 yards, 20 touchdowns and three interceptions while turning 13 carries into 47 yards and two scores. The Bengals will face a Commanders defense that ranks 31st in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (244.8) and 30th in red-zone touchdown rate (71.9 percent).
injuryReports.injury: Burrow (illness) does not have an injury designation ahead of Monday's game against the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Oren Burks
injuryReports.returnComment: Burks has been working through a groin issue for the past couple of weeks, and he aggravated the injury during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday. His placement on IR means he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 20.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Tee Higgins
injuryReports.returnComment: It's a new "injury" for Higgins, but the full participation level suggests it's nothing serious after the wideout was managed late in last Sunday night's blowout win over the Steelers, per Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer. Higgins already has a fantasy-friendly 53 catches (on 73 targets) for 824 yards and six touchdowns through nine games. He's on pace for a career year in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Higgins (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Joe Flacco
injuryReports.returnComment: With the Bengals having built their lead to 20 by the midway point of the fourth quarter, head coach Zac Taylor pulled starter Joe Burrow from the contest and turned to Flacco to run down the clock in the win. The appearance was Flacco's third of the season, but the veteran signal-caller still has yet to attempt a pass.
injuryReports.injury: Flacco took the field for the Bengals' final possession of Sunday's 38-18 win over the Steelers, attempting no passes while handing off to running back Tahj Brooks on all three of his snaps.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Battle
injuryReports.returnComment: Battle ranked second on Cincinnati in stops. One of his six tackles went for a loss, and the 25-year-old also forced a fumble, though it was recovered by the Steelers. Battle has played every defensive snap in seven of the Bengals' nine contests this season, and he's collected 58 tackles and eight defensed passes, including three interceptions.
injuryReports.injury: Battle finished Sunday's 38-18 win over Pittsburgh with six tackles (four solo), one defensed pass and one forced fumble.

injuryReports.name: Demetrius Knight Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Knight led Cincinnati in tackles in the blowout win. The second-year linebacker has recorded exactly eight stops in four of his past five games, and he's finished with at least that tally in all but three of his appearances overall this season. Knight hasn't yet recorded a sack, but he's on pace to blow by his rookie total of 106 stops, as he has 71 tackles across nine games.
injuryReports.injury: Knight finished with eight tackles (six solo) and a defensed pass against the Steelers in a 38-18 victory Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Barrett Carter
injuryReports.returnComment: Carter's tackle tally tied for second-most on the Bengals. The second-year pro has now reached the six-tackle mark in all but one of his nine games this season. Carter leads the Bengals with 74 stops overall, and he's recorded 1.5 sacks, five defensed passes (including an interception) and two forced fumbles.
injuryReports.injury: Carter posted six tackles (two solo) and a defensed pass in Sunday's 38-18 win over Pittsburgh.

injuryReports.name: Drew Sample
injuryReports.returnComment: Sample entered the contest with no catches over his previous two games, but he tied season-high marks in both receptions and targets versus the Steelers. He gave Cincinnati a two-score lead just after the beginning of the second quarter when he hauled in a three-yard TD from Joe Burrow. Sample has two touchdowns over his past four games, but with just five catches for 39 yards during that span, he's almost entirely dependent on getting into the end zone to generate useful fantasy production.
injuryReports.injury: Sample caught all three of his targets for 15 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-18 win against Pittsburgh.

injuryReports.name: Evan McPherson
injuryReports.returnComment: McPherson converted a 24-yard field-goal attempt on the first drive of the game. The kicker proceeded to miss a 43-yarder in the second quarter of the contest, though the miss did not end up mattering to the final result of the game. McPherson is now 13-for-14 on field-goal attempts and 33-for-33 on PATs over nine contests this season.
injuryReports.injury: McPherson made one of his two field-goal attempts and all five PATs in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Dohnte Meyers
injuryReports.returnComment: Meyers reeled in multiple passes for the third straight game, and he was able to secure his first score of the year in the second quarter on a 15-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow. The 26-year-old's 28 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Cincinnati behind Ja'Marr Chase (59), Tee Higgins (51) and Colbie Young (29). With Andrei Iosivas (thumb) nearing a return to action, Meyers may see a sharp drop in offensive opportunities in the near future.
injuryReports.injury: Meyers caught both of his targets for 20 yards and a touchdown while also adding 58 yards as a kick returner during Sunday night's 38-18 win over the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Samaje Perine
injuryReports.returnComment: It looked like Chase Brown found the end zone in the fourth quarter for his third score of the game, but replay assist revealed that his knee came down just short of the goal line. Perine came in on the next play and took the ball for a one-yard touchdown to extend the Bengals' lead to 38-10 following Evan MacPherson's successful extra-point try. It was Perine's third touchdown of the season and first since Week 7 against the Ravens, and over his last five games, he has turned 39 carries into 151 yards (3.9 YPC) and two touchdowns while adding seven catches on as many targets for 44 yards and a score. He'll continue to operate as the Bengals' RB2 behind Brown heading into Week 11 against the Commanders on Monday, Nov. 23.
injuryReports.injury: Perine turned six carries into 14 yards and a touchdown and hauled in all four of his targets for 25 yards during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Tahj Brooks
injuryReports.returnComment: All three of Brooks' carries came during the Bengals' final possession of the fourth quarter, when the team had already built a sizable lead and opted to rest multiple key players, including top running back Chase Brown. Brooks has been active for all nine of the Bengals' games to date but has logged just six carries, all of which have come late in blowout victories. So long as Brown and Samaje Perine are both available, Brooks will continue to see limited playing time on offense.
injuryReports.injury: Brooks carried three times for 12 yards while taking the field for three of the Bengals' 66 offensive snaps in Sunday's 38-18 win over the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Mike Gesicki
injuryReports.returnComment: Gesicki caught six touchdowns in the first seven games of the season, but he's now produced just three grabs for 20 scoreless yards over the past two contests. The fluky touchdown rate was never going to hold up, and Joe Burrow funnels so many of his targets through Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown that there isn't a whole lot more to go around to Cincinnati's ancillary weapons. Gesicki is a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option most weeks despite running a bunch of routes as the de facto slot receiver.
injuryReports.injury: Gesicki caught one pass for nine yards in Sunday night's 38-18 win over the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Amik Robertson
injuryReports.returnComment: Robertson suffered an ankle injury at the team's final practice of the week, so his absence Monday comes as no surprise. In his absence, Mike Sainristil and Quan Martin will both likely operate in more prominent roles at cornerback versus Cincinnati.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Athan Kaliakmanis
injuryReports.returnComment: Kaliakmanis will operate as the No. 3 option at QB once again in Week 11. The 23-year-old will only be eligible to enter the contest if both starter Jayden Daniels and primary backup Marcus Mariota are sidelined.
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
injuryReports.returnComment: The Commanders activated Croskey-Merritt from injured reserve Monday and cleared his designation, guaranteeing his first game action since Week 5. The one question mark that remained in the team's backfield was the status of Rachaad White (heel), but he also is suiting up in Week 11. Croskey-Merrit thus will have to contend with White and Austin Ekeler for touches.
injuryReports.injury: Croskey-Merritt (groin) is listed as active Monday against the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Rachaad White
injuryReports.returnComment: White showed up on the Commanders' Week 11 injury report Friday as limited due to a heel issue and then didn't practice Saturday, leaving him questionable to play Monday. While he's confirmed to be available, he also will be welcoming back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) from IR for the first time since Week 5, which may eat into White's workload.
injuryReports.injury: White (heel) is active for Monday's game against the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Quan Martin
injuryReports.returnComment: Martin's practice reps were limited both Thursday and Friday due to a shoulder issue, but his full session Saturday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Monday night's game. Martin could see an uptick in defensive snaps if defensive back Amik Robertson (ankle) is not cleared to play against Cincinnati.
injuryReports.injury: Martin (shoulder) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Treylon Burks
injuryReports.returnComment: Burks was held out of Friday's practice while managing a foot injury, but he returned Saturday as a full participant, which was enough for him to shed an injury tag for Monday's contest. Over his last six outings, Burks has caught 14 passes on 24 targets for 260 yards and two touchdowns, and he has operated as operated as the Commanders' WR3 since Terry McLaurin suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 6 against the 49ers.
injuryReports.injury: Burks (foot) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Laremy Tunsil
injuryReports.returnComment: Tunsil underwent surgery in August to repair a torn triceps. The left tackle continues to recover, but he likely will not suit up for the Commanders in 2026 unless the team makes a playoff run. Even then, it remains unclear whether Tunsil would be able to return at all before the 2027 season.
injuryReports.injury: Triceps

injuryReports.name: Colson Yankoff
injuryReports.returnComment: Yankoff sat out the Commanders' contest against the Giants in Week 10 because of a knee injury, but it now looks like he's put it behind him. He figures to resume a depth role at tight end in Week 11 against the Bengals.
injuryReports.injury: Yankoff (knee) was a full participant at practice Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Luke McCaffrey
injuryReports.returnComment: Though he's been active for five straight games while the Commanders' receiving depth has taken hits due to season-ending injuries to Terry McLaurin (knee) and Jaylin Lane (ankle), McCaffrey has yet to carve out much of a role on offense. He took the field for a season-high 14 of the Commanders' 69 offensive plays in Week 10 but went without a target. McCaffrey is likely to continue to provide his greatest impact on special teams, where he appears to have settled in as the Commanders' top return man on both kickoffs and punts.
injuryReports.injury: McCaffrey returned two punts for 13 yards and three kickoffs for 58 yards in Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Jeremy Reaves
injuryReports.returnComment: Reaves finished Thursday's game second on the Commanders in tackles behind rookie first-round linebacker Sonny Styles (13), and the former jumped on a loose ball caused by Frankie Luvu in the third quarter that stopped the Giants' red zone drive. Reaves has logged at least five stops in each of the first nine games of the regular season, and the veteran safety is up to 62 tackles (35 solo), four pass defenses and one fumble recovery on the year.
injuryReports.injury: Reaves recorded nine tackles (seven solo), one pass defense and one fumble recovery during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Nick Cross
injuryReports.returnComment: Cross was one of three Commanders players who played all 65 defensive snaps during Thursday's win. He's posted at least six stops in each of his last three outings, and over that span, he has accumulated 23 tackles (12 solo), three pass defenses (including one interception) and one fumble recovery.
injuryReports.injury: Cross finished Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants with six tackles (one solo).

injuryReports.name: Frankie Luvu
injuryReports.returnComment: Luvu stopped the Giants' red zone drive in the third quarter after punching the ball out of the hands of Malik Nabers, and Jeremy Reaves jumped on the loose ball to secure the takeaway for the Commanders. Luvu has played every single snap in each of his last three games, and he has accumulated 51 tackles (21 solo), including 1.0 sacks, one pass defense, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery over his last six outings.
injuryReports.injury: Luvu recorded six tackles (two solo) and a forced fumble during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Sonny Styles
injuryReports.returnComment: Styles once again led the Commanders in stops while playing every single defensive snap. He has logged exactly 13 tackles in four of his last five games and is up to 80 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, four pass defenses (including one interception) and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games. Styles' 80 combined tackles are third-most among rookies behind Anthony Hill (neck) (82) and Arvell Reese (81).
injuryReports.injury: Styles recorded 13 tackles (five solo) during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Drew Stevens
injuryReports.returnComment: Stevens began the scoring in the contest with a 46-yard field goal early in the second period. That ended up being his only FG try of the game, but he made all three of his PATs. Stevens continued what has been a mostly fine rookie campaign -- he's made 17 of 20 field-goal attempts, with all three of his misses coming from 50-plus yards. However, he's just 15-for-18 on point-after tries.
injuryReports.injury: Stevens made his only field-goal attempt and was successful on all three of his extra-point tries in Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Ben Sinnott
injuryReports.returnComment: Sinnott gave the Commanders a lead just before halftime when he reeled in a one-yard touchdown from Jayden Daniels. It was his first TD of the season and the third of his career. Sinnott's four grabs came out of nowhere, as he'd logged just one catch on two targets through his first eight games of the season. He also ranked third among Washington tight ends Thursday with 24 offensive snaps -- behind Chig Okonkwo (41) and John Bates (28) -- so fantasy managers probably don't need to go rushing to the waiver wire to pick him up. With that said, Sinnott may have earned himself more opportunities with Thursday's effort.
injuryReports.injury: Sinnott caught all four of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown Thursday in a 24-21 victory against the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Antonio Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams was a distant second to Stefon Diggs in receiving yards for the Commanders on the night, but like the latter, the former was on the receiving end of one of Jayden Daniels' three touchdown passes. Williams scored from 31 yards out just past the midway point of the third quarter, his first touchdown since way back in Week 1 against the Eagles. Williams hasn't been able to fully take advantage of the absence of Terry McLaurin (knee, IR) as of yet, but Thursday's score is certainly an encouraging sign heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.
injuryReports.injury: Williams secured both targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Austin Ekeler
injuryReports.returnComment: As his final line indicates, Ekeler retained a solid level of involvement in the narrow win, logging a season-high 13 touches. He posted a new season high in receiving yards along the way, and the veteran back has proven to be a solid complement to Rachaad White while Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin, IR) has been sidelined. However, with the latter potentially set to return as soon as Week 11's home matchup against the Bengals, Ekeler could be headed to a reduced role.
injuryReports.injury: Ekeler rushed nine times for 26 yards and brought in all four targets for 26 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Stefon Diggs
injuryReports.returnComment: Diggs paced the Commanders across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his 32-yard catch-and-run touchdown grab over the middle with under a minute remaining sealed the win for Washington. Diggs tied a season high with his catch total while setting a new 2026 high-water mark in receiving yards and targets as well, and the veteran wideout should retain a prominent role throughout the second half of the season with Terry McLaurin (IR, knee) out the rest of the way in 2026. Diggs next takes aim at the Bengals' inconsistent secondary in a Week 11 home matchup on Monday night, Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: Diggs secured six of 10 targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Jayden Daniels
injuryReports.returnComment: It was a up-and-down night for Daniels in the narrow division win, as the third-year quarterback's pair of fourth-quarter interceptions threatened to derail Washington's fortunes. Daniels had the Commanders up by a 17-14 score just past the midway point of the third quarter after tossing one- and 31-yard touchdown passes to Ben Sinnott and Antonio Williams, respectively. However, Daniels subsequently squandered one scoring opportunity by throwing interceptions on back-to-back possessions in the fourth quarter, the first at the Giants' two-yard line. He ultimately made up for it with his game-winning 32-yard scoring strike to Stefon Diggs, marking the quarterback's first three-TD-pass tally of the season. Daniels is up to 1,499 passing yards and a 10:2 TD:INT alongside 280 rushing yards and another pair of scores heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.
injuryReports.injury: Daniels completed 23 of 33 passes for 249 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions and rushed 11 times for 28 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Chig Okonkwo
injuryReports.returnComment: Okonkwo exited in the second quarter due to a back injury, but he was back out there on the field after halftime and was the target on both of Jayden Daniels' two interceptions with less than six minutes remaining in the contest. Overall, Okonkwo's eight targets marked a season high, but he also mustered his fewest receiving yards since Week 4. He'll look to build upon his season-long line of 27-263-0 on 39 targets in the Commanders' next game Monday, Nov. 23 versus the Bengals.
injuryReports.injury: Okonkwo (back) returned to Thursday's eventual 24-21 win at the Giants, finishing with four catches (on eight targets) for 24 yards.
